sources.entry: FunNotch - Puts the MacBook notch to work: media controls, a drag-and-drop file shelf, clipboard history, focus sessions that block sites and apps, and twelve configurable widgets.

summary.one_liner: FunNotch is a free, open-source macOS app that turns the area around the MacBook notch into a panel for media controls, a file shelf, clipboard history, focus sessions, notes, a timer and widgets.
summary.what_it_does: FunNotch places a customizable home grid of widgets in the space beside the MacBook camera notch. It shows now-playing media from Music, Spotify and browsers, with artwork, a spectrum and a seekable progress bar. A shelf holds dragged files until they are dragged out, and it catches new screenshots and finished downloads. Clipboard history is searchable and pinnable, expires entries after 24 hours by default, and skips items marked concealed by password managers. Focus sessions block websites and apps with Pomodoro cycles, and a countdown and stopwatch sit alongside them. The app also replaces the system volume, brightness and keyboard backlight overlays, and on external displays it draws a floating pill instead. The README describes it as having thirteen widgets, a weather scene, battery wattage, calendar and reminders, and two games.
use_cases: see now-playing music in the notch
hold files temporarily while dragging them somewhere
block distracting websites and apps during focus time
replace the macOS volume and brightness overlay
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the releases page or funnotch.xyz, drag FunNotch to Applications, and open it.
On first launch, approve it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (builds are ad-hoc signed).
To build from source: ./build.sh (debug build into build/)
Optional packaging: ./build.sh --universal --package to produce dist/*.dmg and dist/*.zip
notable: Notch-native UI: a non-activating panel that draws widgets, media and tools around the camera cutout
Replaces the system HUD for volume, brightness and keyboard backlight rather than sitting beside it
Focus sessions that actually block sites and apps, with Pomodoro cycles and a streak
Built with swiftc directly, no Xcode project; includes a preview renderer that writes notch states to PNG
Explicitly states no account, no subscription and no telemetry; README lists only three network destinations
caveats: Builds are ad-hoc signed, so macOS blocks the first launch until the user approves it manually; notarized builds need a paid Apple Developer certificate
Self-test requires a GUI session and will not run over plain SSH
Permissions such as Accessibility (for the HUD), Calendar, Camera and Location are needed only for their specific features
Written as a rebuild of TheBoringNotch; the README itself says that project does some things better
